content.title: About
content.content: Reduced‑sodium pepperoni is a traditional Italian‑style sausage made from pork and beef, seasoned with paprika, garlic and spices, but with less salt. It retains the characteristic smoky heat while being more suitable for those watching their sodium intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pepperoni originated in the United States as a variation of salami adapted to American tastes.
The lower‑salt formulation replaces part of the salt with potassium chloride and relies on stronger spices for flavor.
Pepperoni is most commonly used as a pizza topping, but also works well in sandwiches, salads and snack platters.
Traditional pepperoni gets its bright red color from paprika and sometimes artificial dyes; reduced‑sodium versions often use natural colorants.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Pepperoni provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports the nervous system and the formation of red blood cells.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: The iron in meat helps maintain normal hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Reduced sodium
items.content: Lower salt content makes this product more suitable for people with hypertension or cardiovascular concerns.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to pork or beef.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Like most cured sausages, pepperoni contains saturated fats and should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain brands may contain nitrites or other preservatives that can be a concern for sensitive consumers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice pepperoni thinly and add it to pizza, pasta, salads, sandwiches, or simply pan‑fry it as a snack. To reduce excess fat, blot the cooked slices with a paper towel.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep pepperoni in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C. Once opened, it is best used within 2–3 weeks. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
